description.text: Pulp can be either recycled or virgin pulp. Recycled pulp is made from used materials, such as printing and writing papers, newsprint, packaging and other types of carton board, and then processed by chemicals in order to remove printing inks and other elements. Virgin pulp can be manufactured from a number of raw materials, such as wood, bagasse and bamboo, and it is classified based on the type of wood or fiber derived from the corresponding raw material as well as the processing system used and whether the pulp will be bleached. Bleached pulp is used for several purposes, including printing and writing, specialty, packaging paperboard and tissue papers. Unbleached pulp has a brown color and is used in the production of packages, corrugated board, paperboard, packaging papers, bags and tissue. The most common raw material that we use to produce paper is wood pulp. Different tree species yield different fiber characteristics and, consequently, different paper attributes such as strength, softness and opacity. There are two types of wood pulp: hardwood pulp and softwood pulp. Hardwood pulp is produced using hardwood trees, such as eucalyptus, aspen, birch, acacia, maple, oaks, beech trees and poplars, which have shorter fibers.

about.description_short: Suzano is the world's largest pulp supplier, a major paper and packaging producer in the Americas, and one of Brazil's biggest employers. Driven by a deep commitment to sustainability and innovation, Suzano produces responsibly-grown raw materials that are exported to more than 100 countries around the world. These are used to make everyday items that reach more than two billion people, including toilet paper and tissue, packaging, printing and writing paper, personal hygiene products, and textiles. Founded in Brazil over 100 years ago, today Suzano operates across Latin America, North America, Europe and Asia. The company's shares are listed on the B3 in São Paulo (SUZB3) and the New York Stock Exchange (SUZ).

analysis_md:
# SUZ — Suzano S.A.
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-18. Brazilian pulp & paper, 20-F IFRS filer reporting in BRL (engine FX-converts at period-end ECB rates); NYSE ADS at a 1:1 ratio to the common share. In scope: market cap $10.538B at $8.50 (nasdaq_quote_api).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.py output, fundamentals.json, or segments.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The world's largest hardwood (eucalyptus) pulp producer, vertically integrated from its own plantations through mills, ports and logistics into paper. FY2025 revenue mix (segments.json, BRL): market pulp R$37,816,141,000 (75.5% of revenue), printing & writing paper R$8,260,804,000 (16.5%), the rest paperboard/tissue/other. The Cerrado mill at Ribas do Rio Pardo — the world's largest single pulp line, 2.55Mt/yr, started July 2024 — lifted total market-pulp capacity ~20% to ~13.4Mt and is expected to run above nominal capacity (2.57Mt guided for 2026, ~2.7Mt from 2027, per company investor materials). ## Moat: 5/10 — moderate (structural cost advantage, zero pricing power)
Justification: World's largest hardwood pulp producer with a structural cost advantage — own fast-growing eucalyptus plantations, integrated logistics and the Cerrado mill put it at the low end of the global cost curve (pulp cash cost R$817/t in FY2025, lowest since 2021) — but it is a pure price-taker in a commodity: gross margin swung 50.2% (FY2022) to 32.4% (FY2025) with the pulp cycle, and roic_proxy fell from 17.9% (FY2022) to 8.5% / 9.9% / 6.8% (FY2023/24/25), i.e. recent returns sit around, not well above, the cost of capital through this part of the cycle. ROIC and margin history are from fundamentals.json (roic_proxy: FY2021 17.7%, FY2022 17.9%, FY2023 8.5%, FY2024 9.9%, FY2025 6.8%; gross margin FY2021 49.7%, FY2022 50.2%, FY2023 36.9%, FY2024 42.2%, FY2025 32.4%). A moat above 6 would need returns that stay well above the cost of capital through the cycle; Suzano's do not — its edge shows up as surviving troughs at lower cost than peers, not as pricing power.
- FOR: structural cost advantage — own eucalyptus plantations with short harvest cycles close to the mills, integrated logistics and ports (pulp cash cost R$817/t FY2025, lowest since 2021); scale — world's largest hardwood pulp producer, Cerrado added 2.55Mt/yr (~20%, total ~13.4Mt) and cut consolidated pulp cash cost 6% in 2024 to R$828/t; vertical integration into paper/paperboard/tissue plus the 2024 US paperboard acquisition diversifies the pulp-only exposure (market pulp still ~75% of FY2025 revenue); through-cycle cash generation — OE positive 5/5 last fiscal years, including the 2023 pulp-price trough.
- AGAINST: commodity price-taker — pulp price is set by the market (China demand, industry capacity), gross margin ranged 32–50% in five years on price alone; returns are cycle-determined (roic_proxy 17.9% peak → 6.8% FY2025); high leverage amplifies the cycle (net debt $14.536B, 8.1x normalized OE); BRL/USD exposure both ways — USD-linked revenues vs BRL costs, and USD debt/hedge marks drove the FY2024 net loss (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE); new industry capacity (including Cerrado's own tonnes) pressures the price it takes, and eucalyptus monoculture draws standing environmental scrutiny.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — engine 5.4.0 final run (2026-10-18)
Growth recalibration (written reason): the engine's blended growth is 16.66% and is not usable as a scenario anchor for this company. Its components (key_numbers.md) are rev CAGR 5y 9.30%, rev CAGR 3y −0.99%, latest rev YoY 19.37%, OE/share CAGR 2y 50.10%. The latest YoY is an FX artifact — USD-converted revenue rose 19.37% while BRL revenue rose only ~5.7% (R$47.40B → R$50.12B, fundamentals.json), because the period-end BRL rate moved 0.16169 → 0.18256. The OE/share CAGR is a capex-cliff artifact — it runs from the FY2023 trough ($0.90) through the end of Cerrado construction capex to FY2025 ($1.98); that step-up cannot repeat. And the Cerrado volume step (+20% capacity) is a one-off level shift, largely already in the FY2025 base (first full year), with only the above-nominal creep (2.57Mt in 2026, ~2.7Mt from 2027) still ahead. Honest nominal growth for a mature commodity producer with modest volume creep is mid-single digits. Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (−0.2466 / −0.1666 / −0.1066 / −0.0566 / −0.0066 vs the blend) to −8 / 0 / **6** / 11 / 16%. Sanity check against recent prints: the base start (6%) sits on the FY2025 BRL revenue print (+5.7%) and below the USD print; the bull start (11%) is below the latest USD revenue YoY (19.37%) and far below the latest OE/share YoY — justified because both of those prints are FX/capex-cliff artifacts, not run-rate growth; the super-bear start (−8%) reflects a pulp downcycle (OE/share fell ~47% in FY2023 vs FY2022 on price). Probabilities 15/30/30/17/8 — heavier bear weight than default for a levered cyclical (see TIER_BAND / HIGH_NET_DEBT). OE multipliers 0.70/0.88/1.00/1.10/1.25: the bear/super-bear multipliers are widened vs default because the filed OE range is wide (FY2023 OE/share $0.90 is 0.62x the $1.45 median base). - **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count −2.33%/yr): already credited via the growth adjustment to the revenue components only (v5.4); not double-counted in the verdict.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2024): found and one-off in nature. FY2024 net income was −R$7,045M (20-F income statement) while OCF was R$20.60B (fundamentals.json), because the income statement carried monetary/exchange variations of −R$15,885M and derivative losses of −R$9,113M — non-cash mark-to-market on USD-denominated debt and hedge positions as the BRL fell sharply in 2024 — partly offset by a deferred-tax credit of +R$7,432M (all figures from the FY2024 20-F income statement). The company's own release confirms the loss had no immediate cash impact (cash effect only at debt/hedge maturity). The OCF-based conservative OE used throughout is not contaminated by these marks.
- **FX_CONVERTED**: BRL reporting converted at period-end ECB rates (recorded in dcf_numbers.json); flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average — a screening simplification, and the reason the USD revenue YoY (19.37%) overstates the BRL print (~5.7%). Noted, and the growth recalibration above is built on the BRL prints.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED** (x1.0): see OVERRIDE — 1 ADS = 1 common share per the filer's own 20-F; no scaling effect.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:sbc**: see OVERRIDE — gap, decision, anchor, band check and measured impact are all recorded in fields (judgment.json, dcf_numbers.json overrides_applied/override_impact, overrides_registry.json), not just here.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY OE/share $1.98 vs 3-yr median $1.45): both are distorted in opposite directions, and the median is the safer base. The latest FY is flattered by the capex trough — PPE capex fell to R$4.58B in FY2025 (fundamentals.json) from R$9.19B (FY2024) and R$11.67B (FY2023) as Cerrado construction ended, and the PPE tag does not capture all forestry/biological-asset investment, so FY2025 OE overstates a steady-state year. The median (FY2024) is penalized by still carrying Cerrado build capex, so it understates steady state. Keeping the median errs conservative; a latest-FY base would print a higher IRR and is part of the method range in Thoughts.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.83x): real — a commodity producer's outcome range IS this wide. Confidence is low, probabilities are bear-weighted, and the verdict is sized to the bear end.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 8.11x normalized OE): balance sheet from the filing (dcf_numbers.json): net debt $14.536B on the basis LongtermBorrowings + CurrentBorrowingsAndCurrentPortionOfNoncurrentBorrowings, plus lease liabilities $1.265B, against equity $8.024B (financials_history.csv, USD converted). On the company's own adjusted-EBITDA definition leverage was 3.2x (USD) at FY2025 and 3.4x at 2Q26 — manageable for a pulp major in normal prices, but 8.1x the engine's OE means a deep price trough reaches the equity fast; that is why the super-bear case carries 15% and a 0.70 multiplier.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear B 16.37% vs bull S 27.96%): the verdict spans tiers, so any position is sized to the bear end — the final tier stays A by numbers (no tier_override), with the one-liner and verdict explicitly sizing it like a B.

## My thoughts / overlay
- Method range: the two defensible bases bracket the answer. On the normalized median ($1.45) the weighted IRR is 21.24% (Tier A). On a trough definition (FY2023's $0.90/share persisting) the name would not clear 15% at all; on the latest-FY base ($1.98) it would print well into A/S territory. The median is the honest middle, and the 45% combined super-bear+bear probability is the price of the cyclicality.
- The capex definition is the biggest modeling caveat after pulp price itself: the engine's OE charges only the PPE-purchases tag (FY2025 R$4.58B). Suzano's total investment including forestry/biological assets runs materially higher (it reported R$17.1B invested in 2024 including the Cerrado build, vs R$9.19B on the PPE tag that year). A full-capex OE definition would lower every year's OE and compress the IRR — pass 2 forensic territory, flagged here, not silently fixed in pass 1.
- FX cuts both ways and is not in the scenarios except through the growth recalibration: BRL appreciation squeezes BRL margins on USD-linked pulp (2Q26 EBITDA/t fell 12% YoY partly on FX), while BRL depreciation inflates the USD-debt marks that produced FY2024's paper loss.
- Margin of safety on the final numbers: weighted IV@15% sits 52.5% above the $8.50 price, and even the bear case ($9.41) sits above it — but the super-bear IV ($5.35) sits 37% below it, and with 8.1x leverage the super-bear is not a tail curiosity for a pulp producer; 2023 already printed an OE/share 0.62x the base used here.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: A** (by numbers; weighted IRR 21.24% on the normalized median base — sized like a B per TIER_BAND: bear-case tier B, super-bear IV below the price, confidence low)
- Confidence: **Low** (IFRS/FX-converted flows, median-not-TTM base, SBC by estimate override, 4.83x scenario spread, 8.11x net debt to normalized OE)
- One-liner: World's largest, lowest-cost hardwood pulp producer, moat 5/10 — Tier A by numbers on the normalized median base ($1.45/ADS): weighted IRR 21.2%, IV@15% $12.96 vs $8.50 price — but a levered commodity price-taker (net debt 8.1x normalized OE; bear case is Tier B at 16.4% IRR and the super-bear IV of $5.35 sits below the price), so size it like a B.
